Marvel Studios chief Kevin Feige is paying tribute to the late Patrick Stewart , who starred as Professor Charles Xavier since 2000’s “X-Men.”
“I’ll never forget the first time I saw Sir Patrick Stewart on the set of the first X-Men,” said Feige, producer and president of Marvel Studios, in a statement shared after news broke that Stewart died on Wednesday at age 86. “After years of knowing him as the inimitable Captain Picard, I was in awe — and he turned out to be everything I had seen on screen and more: brilliant, charming, warm, generous, with a quiet strength and gravitas.” Related Stories ‘Paper Plane,’ ‘Helicopter’ and ‘Old Bogus Massacre’ Among Austin Film Festival Script and Film Competition Award Winners (EXCLUSIVE) Pink Film Veteran Zeze Takahisa Champions Original Stories at Tokyo Masterclass

“Away from the cameras, he was even more remarkable, with a wonderfully sharp sense of humor,” Feige continued. “It was a true privilege to know him and to work with him. His legacy lives on not only in decades of extraordinary work, but in the many, many people he mentored. He will be deeply missed.”
Stewart has appeared as Professor X in nine movies over more than 25 years, including the original Fox trilogy (“X-Men,” “X2: X-Men United” and “X-Men: The Last Stand”), as well as 2014’s “X-Men: Days of Future Past” and 2017’s “Logan,” plus Marvel Studios’ “Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness” in 2022. Stewart is set to reprise his role in “ Avengers: Doomsday ,” in theaters on Dec. 18. The Marvel movie marks Stewart’s final on-screen appearance.
Marvel Studios also released a statement memorializing the legendary actor for bringing Charles Xavier to life with “extraordinary grace, intelligence, and humanity” and “defining the character for generations of fans.”
“He was a singular talent, a generous collaborator, and a true gentleman,” the statement reads. “Our hearts go out to his wife Sunny, his children, his friends, and the countless fans around the world whose lives he touched with his art.”
All of us at Marvel Studios are deeply saddened by the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart. Sir Patrick brought Professor Charles Xavier to life with extraordinary grace, intelligence, and humanity, defining the character for generations of fans, from X- Men to Logan to Avengers:… pic.twitter.com/ZQoqYnSngs
“Logan” director James Mangold praised Stewart as “a brilliant and tireless actor from stage to screen to TV and back again, as a great collaborator, gentle soul and friend to everyone.” Anthony and Joe Russo, directors of “Avengers: Doomsday,” also shared their gratitude for working with Stewart, whom they described as one of their “childhood heroes.”
“A legendary actor with an unmistakable presence, and an unmatched integrity,” the filmmakers shared . “Thank you for entertaining all of us, sir. And for teaching us humanity, both on and off the screen. Sending our love to your family, friends, and fans around the world.”
“X-Men” director Bryan Singer posted on Instagram to share some photos, saying, “It’s been a while since I last posted, but Patrick Stewart’s passing has brought back decades of memories, and I wanted to share a few candid photographs from our time together. First, my heart goes out to his wonderful wife, Sunny.
Singer continued, “I could never recount all the experiences Patrick and I shared, both professionally and personally, in a single post. He was far more than a cast member and a friend. He was a teacher. Every time I watched Patrick approach a role, whether onstage or on set, I learned something. His command of language, his understanding of character, the precision with which he could deliver an emotion or change the pace of a scene. He possessed a grace and confidence that only a lifetime devoted to the craft could produce, and he made even the most difficult performances seem effortless.
“But beyond his extraordinary talent, Patrick was also a wonderfully fun and adventurous man. One memory still makes me laugh. Knowing what an enormous Star Trek fan I was, Patrick invited me to dinner at his home. What he neglected to mention was that William Shatner would be joining us. I completely freaked out! Patrick knew exactly what he was doing,” Singer said.
With “Doomsday” as Stewart’s final film role, Marvel fans can expect the movie and its global press tour to take on a more reverential tone, with many of the actor’s longtime collaborators and friends, like Hugh Jackman (who called Stewart a “tremendous friend and man” in a heartfelt post) and Ian McKellen, continuing to pay tribute to his legacy.
Rebecca Romijn, who co-starred with Stewart in the “X-Men” movies and is also a part of the “Star Trek” universe, shared a teary video on Instagram .
“I feel so grateful to have known him for the last 25 years, and to have been in his orbit… both as a fellow mutant and as a fellow member of Starfleet,” Romijn said. “He was positively delicious, hilarious, naughty, incredible sense of humor, and that booming voice of his that always spoke to the very back of the room, as every classically trained Shakespearean great needs to master, has always been an inspiration. I send my condolences to his family, and I’ll miss my friend dearly. Rest in peace, Patrick.”
Indeed, like his Marvel family, Stewart’s “Star Trek” crew are mourning, too. Stewart originated the character of Capt. Jean-Luc Picard in 1987 and played him on and off until 2023. Among those who’ve paid tribute are George Takei, Wil Wheaton, Jonathan Frakes, “Star Trek: Picard” co-creators Alex Kurtzman and Akiva Goldsman and fellow USS Enterprise captain William Shatner.
